title: Sheaf quotient by an ideal acting through global sections
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], with object universe $c$ and morphism universe $v$, and let $A$ be a sheaf of commutative rings with values in universe $\max(c,v,r)$. Put $G=\Gamma(\mathcal C,A)$, the ring of compatible families on all site objects, with pointwise commutative ring operations. Let $P$ be any commutative ring, let $\rho:P\to G$ be a ring homomorphism and let $I\subseteq P$ be an ideal. Evaluation at $U$ gives $\rho_U:P\to A(U)$; put $J_0(U)=I A(U)=\operatorname{Ideal.map}(\rho_U,I)$. Restrictions preserve these ideals and induce identity- and composition-compatible maps on $A(U)/J_0(U)$. Define $A/IA$ to be the ring sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of the presheaf $U\mapsto A(U)/J_0(U)$, and $q:A\to A/IA$ to be the sectionwise quotient map followed by the sheafification unit. Ring sheafification exists in the stated ambient universe. Thus the ideal relations are imposed locally; no claim that the sectionwise quotient is already a sheaf is made. The induced map $\Gamma(q):G\to\Gamma(\mathcal C,A/IA)$ applies $q_U$ componentwise to a compatible family. It kills $IG=\operatorname{Ideal.map}(\rho,I)$. Define the canonical comparison $v:G/IG\to\Gamma(\mathcal C,A/IA)$ to be its unique quotient lift, and endow the target with the $G/IG$-algebra structure given by this very $v$. All these constructions retain the specified maps, with no finite-generation, flatness or reducedness assumption.
